data.name: Pinterest static format comparison v10
data.objective: Compare clean text-free editorial Pins with equally product-faithful static Pins carrying one restrained editorial headline, using attributable outbound clicks as the primary outcome.
data.hypothesis: A tasteful four-to-seven-word editorial headline will improve feed comprehension and qualified curiosity without turning the image into an ad template.
successCriteria: Headline and no-headline arms retain identical truth, taste, and anti-template gates.
Each public Pin has a unique format-tagged canonical tracking URL and durable production receipt.
The first 12-Pin cohort is compared on impressions, saves, Pin clicks, Pinterest outbound clicks, attributable site sessions, and downstream product clicks after seven days.
constraints: At most two public Pins per local calendar day and at most one per scheduled slot.
Stop after 12 qualifying public Pins until the cohort receives a seven-day review.
No video generation, paid tools, paid distribution, Sandbox publication, account mutation, or weak quota-filling.
Pinterest v3 and Sandbox remain permanently excluded from traffic evidence.
